---
title: "Five-week study plan"
---

The course has 25 study units. Each includes a lecture, exercises, and a quiz.
Worked examples introduce the tools; later tasks apply them to another question
or dataset. Save your results and check that you can reproduce them after
closing the applications.

## Weekly sequence and checkpoints

| Week | Main work | Checkpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — Files and computers | Save, find, and reopen files; folders and paths; memory and storage; terminal navigation; archives and text search | Find the same folder in graphical and terminal views, inspect an archive, and package your findings |
| 2 — R and reports | Objects and vectors; importing tables; units and calculations; plots; R Markdown | Run saved code from the top and render a report from its source |
| 3 — Measurements and variation | Data cleaning; missing values; mean, variance, and SD; group summaries; independent units; uncertainty | Explain counts and units, distinguish spread from uncertainty, and show individual observations in a report |
| 4 — Comparisons and lines | Independent and paired comparisons; effects, intervals, and p-values; calibration; fitted lines | Explain the study design, calculate a comparison or prediction, and describe its limits |
| 5 — Reproduce and transfer | Local and remote projects; data representations; an integrated study; debugging | Package source, inputs, and outputs together, then render from a new location |

## Working through a topic

1. Open the lecture and work through its examples.
2. Complete the exercises, saving the named files in your course project.
3. Check the results against the supplied values or hints.
4. Use the topic quiz to check your understanding; open its hints and answers
   when needed.
5. Reopen your saved work and reproduce a result in a fresh session.

All exercises can be completed independently. Where a task offers biological
and chemistry contexts, choose one route. The exercise supplies the definitions,
quantities, units, and formulas for its calculations.

## Getting help and reviewing

Bring the exact error, the relevant filename, and the last successful step to a
support session. For review, use the weekly quizzes or repeat a workflow from
its raw inputs without following the worked example.

Start with [files and folders](week1/01-files.qmd), consult the
[course overview](overview.qmd), or return to the [weekly route](index.qmd).
